source.summary: Marcus is a senior PM at a B2B construction-SaaS firm who calls personas and journey maps dead artifacts and judges everything by whether it changes a decision. He runs lean: hypotheses live in the Linear ticket, two or three quotes are enough evidence, and his real work is making the roadmap defensible in a 45-minute exec review. He wants AI theme-and-quote surfacing but would never open an auto-persona, and anything new must live inside Linear, not become a sixth silo.

nuggets.text: Aha! is the company standard but his real working roadmap is a Linear project with a view he trusts.
nuggets.quote: my real working roadmap is a Linear project with a view I trust.

nuggets.text: He listens to Gong recordings of sales calls at one and a half speed on the train.
nuggets.quote: Gong recordings from sales calls, I listen to those at one and a half speed on the train.

nuggets.text: His real persona is a Slack channel of customer champions who reply in forty minutes.
nuggets.quote: That's my persona. A real person who replies in forty minutes.

nuggets.text: The commissioned personas are dead artifacts that went in a folder and nobody opens.
nuggets.quote: They're dead artifacts. That's my phrase.

nuggets.text: The printed onboarding journey map is a poster on a Berlin office wall that he has never seen anyone look at.
nuggets.quote: It is on a wall in the Berlin office and I've never seen anyone look at it.

nuggets.text: He looks at the real journey as an Amplitude funnel: where people drop between sign-up and first published schedule.
nuggets.quote: The actual journey I look at in Amplitude: where do people drop between sign-up and first published schedule.

nuggets.text: A journey map with emotions and little smiley faces is something he cannot act on.
nuggets.quote: A map with emotions, little smiley faces, I can't act on.

nuggets.text: He argues the artifact is not the point; the point is whether it changes a decision, else why maintain it.
nuggets.quote: The point is decisions. Does it change a decision? If not, why maintain it.

nuggets.text: Their personas have been updated zero times in eighteen months, which to him means they were not load-bearing.
nuggets.quote: Ours has been updated zero times in eighteen months. And I don't think that's a failure. It means they weren't load-bearing.

nuggets.text: Each Linear initiative has three lines at the top: the problem, the bet and the metric.
nuggets.quote: Each initiative in Linear has three lines at the top: the problem, the bet, the metric.

nuggets.text: He pastes two or three representative quotes and a call link into the Linear ticket, and considers that enough.
nuggets.quote: I paste two or three representative quotes into the Linear ticket and a link to the call. Two or three. That's enough.

nuggets.text: He has seen BAs want every claim linked to a source with IDs and a matrix, which he considers overkill.
nuggets.quote: I've heard BAs I've worked with want every claim to link to a source, with IDs and a matrix. I think that's overkill.

nuggets.text: If a decision is wrong he finds out from the metric, not from the footnote.
nuggets.quote: If a decision is wrong we find out from the metric, not from the footnote.

nuggets.text: He owns the roadmap fully; where he saw a BA own it, it turned into a requirements list, because a roadmap is a strategy argument.
nuggets.quote: I've worked at a place where the BA owned the roadmap and it turned into a requirements list. A roadmap is a strategy argument. That's PM work.

nuggets.text: Every quarter he defends the roadmap in a 45-minute review with the CEO, CFO, head of sales and head of customer success.
nuggets.quote: Every quarter there's a roadmap review with the CEO, CFO, head of sales, head of customer success. I have forty-five minutes.

nuggets.text: Instead of the dates the CFO and sales want, he gives confidence bands: committed, likely, exploring.
nuggets.quote: The CFO wants dates. Sales wants dates. I give them confidence bands instead: committed, likely, exploring.

nuggets.text: He wants a one-pager stating what they are betting on and the one number that tells them it is working.
nuggets.quote: A one-pager that says here's what we're betting on and here's the one number that tells us if it's working.

nuggets.text: To answer why-this-not-that he rebuilds a demand spreadsheet of who asked and revenue at stake every quarter, about six hours.
nuggets.quote: here are the nine customers who asked, here's the revenue at stake. I do that in a spreadsheet right now. A spreadsheet I rebuild every quarter. That's maybe six hours the week before.

nuggets.text: What feeds his prioritization is demand evidence, not archetypes.
nuggets.quote: Show me demand, not archetypes.

nuggets.text: He could use the theme-and-quote part, noting Gong already does a flavor of it.
nuggets.quote: The theme-and-quote part I could use. Gong already does a flavor of it.

nuggets.text: He would never open an auto-generated persona, would not read it, and would not pay for it.
nuggets.quote: Auto-persona? I'd never open it. The tool can make it, I just won't read it. So I wouldn't pay for it.

nuggets.text: His stack works and a new tool is a new silo: another login, another thing people forget to update, another license to justify to finance.
nuggets.quote: A new tool is a new silo. It's another login, another thing people forget to update, another license I have to justify to finance in January.

nuggets.text: For him to consider it, it would have to live inside Linear or sit on top of it; if it is a destination he will not go.
nuggets.quote: It'd have to live inside Linear, or sit on top of it so that I never go there. If it's a destination, I won't go.

nuggets.text: A stale tool is worse than no tool, because people trust it.
nuggets.quote: a stale tool is worse than no tool, because people trust it.

nuggets.text: For a team total under about a hundred a month he would adopt it without asking; over three hundred finance gets involved and he says no.
nuggets.quote: If the team total is under, I don't know, a hundred a month, I'd just do it without asking. Over three hundred, finance gets involved, and I'd say no.

nuggets.text: He wants something that changes what he does Monday morning, not a place for artifacts: artifacts are the hobby, decisions the job.
nuggets.quote: Build something that changes what I do on Monday morning. Artifacts are the hobby; decisions are the job.
